questions.q: What does Defender for Office 365 actually protect?
options: SaaS application usage patterns across any cloud app
Email and collaboration tools, such as Exchange Online, SharePoint, OneDrive, and Teams
Only the Windows endpoint operating system
Only on-prem Active Directory domain controllers
questions.explain: Defender for Office 365 (MDO) is the Defender XDR workload focused on email and Microsoft 365 collaboration tools.

questions.q: What makes Safe Links different from checking a URL only once when an email is delivered?
options: It only works on attachments, never on links
It re-checks the destination against current threat intelligence at the moment someone actually clicks the link
It deletes every link from every email automatically, regardless of content
It checks links exactly once per calendar month on a fixed schedule
questions.explain: A link can be clean at delivery and weaponized later; Safe Links re-checks it at click-time so a later-weaponized page still gets blocked.

questions.q: How does Safe Attachments determine whether a file is malicious?
options: It asks the recipient to decide whether the file looks safe
It only checks the file's name against a list of banned words
It relies solely on the file's reported size in kilobytes
It detonates the attachment in an isolated sandbox and watches what it actually does before delivering the message
questions.explain: Safe Attachments opens the file in a sandbox and observes its behavior, catching payloads that only activate when opened.

questions.q: Why does Business Email Compromise (BEC) require a different kind of defense than Safe Links or Safe Attachments?
options: BEC only targets Linux servers, which Safe Links does not scan
BEC is not a real email-based attack and requires no defense at all
BEC is pure social engineering with no malware or link involved, so impersonation detection and mailbox intelligence are needed instead
BEC always includes a malicious attachment, so Safe Attachments alone is sufficient
questions.explain: Since BEC has nothing for a sandbox or link-check to inspect, anti-phishing policies rely on impersonation detection and mailbox intelligence instead.

questions.q: What does mailbox intelligence help anti-phishing policies detect?
options: Whether an attachment has been digitally signed by Microsoft
A message that claims to be from a known sender but doesn't match that sender's normal mail patterns
The exact physical location of the email server that sent the message
The total number of recipients on a distribution list
questions.explain: Mailbox intelligence learns a mailbox's normal senders and patterns, helping flag an impersonation that doesn't match that baseline.
